material_systems.name: Acrylic Stain-Block Primer for Soffit Repaint
material_systems.description: 100% acrylic exterior stain-blocking primer for previously painted soffit surfaces where existing paint has failed or peeled, exposing bare wood substrate. Primary RP primer for exposed wood areas on SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT and SS_EXT_PEELING conditions. Spot prime when localized failure; full prime on SS_EXT_PEELING. Not used on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (skip prime) or SS_EXT_CHALKING (use chalk-binding instead). Previously painted substrate absorbs less than NC bare wood -- higher coverage per gallon than NC acrylic primer. Overhead application increases waste ~10%.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
products.notes: Stain-blocking adhesion primer for bare wood areas on soffit where paint has failed or peeled. Seals exposed wood grain. Spot prime scraped/sanded bare areas when localized; full prime when SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread bare exposure. Distinct from NC SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_ACRYLIC which is for bare substrate -- this is for existing paint with adhesion concerns on surrounding areas.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped bare wood areas; full prime if widespread bare exposure
prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_PEELING: full surface prime after heavy scrape to sound substrate

material_systems.notes: RP-SPECIFIC primer system. Same product family as SYS_PRIMER_EXT_ACRYLIC_STAINBLOCK from SF_WINDOW_EXT_RP and SYS_EXT_TRRP_PRIMER_ACRYLIC from SF_TRIM_EXT_RP. Adapted for SF-based soffit coverage model. Overhead application increases material waste ~10%.

material_systems.name: Chalk-Binding Primer for Chalking Exterior Soffit
material_systems.description: Low-viscosity chalk-binding conditioner primer that penetrates and binds loose chalk residue on exterior soffit surfaces. MANDATORY for SS_EXT_CHALKING regardless of substrate material type. Full surface application required -- chalk binding must be uniform. Apply after low-pressure wash and 24-48 hour dry time. Higher material consumption than standard acrylic primer due to aggressive absorption by chalk residue. Chalking is less common on soffit than siding/trim (sheltered from UV) but occurs on south-facing and exposed eave-edge soffits.

products.notes: MANDATORY for chalking soffit surfaces. Penetrates and binds loose chalk particles left after low-pressure wash. Do NOT skip -- topcoat adhesion failure guaranteed without chalk-binding step. Full surface application required regardless of substrate material. Overhead application reduces efficiency -- thicker-bodied product drips more than standard primer when applied overhead.

material_systems.notes: RP-SPECIFIC primer system. Same product family as SYS_PRIMER_EXT_CHALK_BINDING from SF_WINDOW_EXT_RP and SF_TRIM_EXT_RP. Chalk-binding primer has lower coverage (~200-300 SF/gal) due to thicker body required for chalk penetration. Overhead waste factor applies.

material_systems.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer for Bare Fiber Cement Soffit
material_systems.description: Alkali-resistant acrylic masonry primer for exposed bare fiber cement soffit areas where paint has failed or peeled, revealing substrate. Required for bare/damaged fiber cement (pH 13.0) to prevent saponification. In RP context, applied as spot primer on exposed bare fiber cement areas only -- not full surface unless extensive failure. Reuses NC system unchanged -- same product, same chemistry, spot application mode in RP.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec Masonry & Stucco Primer
products.notes: MANDATORY on exposed bare fiber cement areas. Prevents saponification (alkaline burn) of latex binders at pH 13.0. Standard acrylic primer is NOT suitable for bare fiber cement. Spot prime exposed areas in RP context. Bare FC soffit in RP typically occurs at panel edges and joint failures where paint has peeled back to substrate.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime exposed bare fiber cement areas
prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_PEELING: spot prime all exposed fiber cement areas; full prime if extensive failure

material_systems.notes: Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_ALKALI unchanged. Same product, spot application mode in RP. Coverage profile uses COV_SFRP_PRIMER_ALKALI_SPOT (SF-based, fraction of total soffit area). Overhead waste factor applies.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Vinyl Soffit
material_systems.description: Specialized PVC bonding primer for exposed vinyl soffit areas where paint has failed or peeled. MANDATORY for adhesion on vinyl substrate -- standard acrylic and alkyd primers will NOT bond to vinyl. In RP context, spot prime bare vinyl areas where prior coating has failed. Vinyl is non-porous -- bonding primer provides chemical adhesion to PVC surface. Must clean vinyl surface and scuff-sand before application. Recoat within 1 week or primer loses flexibility. Reuses NC system unchanged.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Insl-X Stix Bonding Primer
products.notes: MANDATORY on exposed bare vinyl areas. Standard primers will NOT adhere to vinyl -- peeling within 6-12 months. Scuff-sand vinyl with 220-grit before application. Spot prime exposed areas in RP context. Recoat within 1 week or bonding primer loses flexibility and becomes brittle. Only 100% acrylic latex binders compatible.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime exposed vinyl areas after scuff-sand and cleaning
prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_PEELING: spot prime all exposed vinyl areas; full prime if extensive failure

material_systems.notes: Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_BONDING unchanged. Same product, spot application mode in RP. Non-porous vinyl provides consistent, higher coverage than wood. Overhead waste factor applies.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Soffit Paint
material_systems.description: Standard production 100% acrylic exterior paint with mildewcide for soffit repaint at QT2/QT3. Flat to satin sheen only. NOT fine-finish -- standard exterior field coating. Mildew-resistant formulation is recommended for all soffit work due to sheltered, shaded, moisture-prone conditions. Once surface is prepped and primed, finish application is identical to NC. QT2: single finish coat. QT3: 2 finish coats.

products.notes: Standard residential exterior acrylic. Flat to satin sheen only (overhead surfaces show imperfections at higher sheen). QT2: single finish coat on prepped/primed surface. QT3: 2 coats standard. Mildew-resistant formulation recommended -- soffit is the highest-risk exterior surface for mildew growth. Apply thin coats overhead to prevent sag.

material_systems.notes: Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_SFIT_FINISH_STANDARD unchanged. Same product, same application. Prepped and primed RP surface is equivalent to NC primed surface for finish coat purposes.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Acrylic Soffit Paint
material_systems.description: Premium 100% acrylic exterior paint with enhanced mildew resistance for QT4 soffit repaint. Superior color retention, fade resistance, and mildew resistance. Light sand between coats (220-grit). Flat to satin sheen. NOT fine-finish -- premium field coating. 2 finish coats standard.

products.product_type: Premium 100% Acrylic Exterior with Enhanced Mildew Resistance
products.notes: Premium materials with superior color retention and mildew resistance. Light sand between coats (220-grit). Raking light inspection before second coat. Flat to satin sheen. Premium formulation has higher solids -- slightly lower coverage per gallon. Apply thin coats overhead to prevent sag.

material_systems.notes: Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_SFIT_FINISH_PREMIUM unchanged. Mildew-resistant formulation is especially important for sheltered soffit surfaces on north-facing and shaded elevations.

material_systems.name: Solar-Reflective Paint for Vinyl Soffit
material_systems.description: CONDITIONAL: Required when vinyl substrate AND color LRV < 55. IR-reflective acrylic with Complex Inorganic Color Pigments (CICPs) prevents thermal distortion of vinyl panels. HARD STOP -- standard dark paint on vinyl causes warping at ~165 deg F. Only 100% acrylic latex binders. Color palette more limited than standard lines. Reuses NC system unchanged.

products.product_type: IR-Reflective Acrylic with Complex Inorganic Color Pigments (CICPs)
example_products: Benjamin Moore Colors for Vinyl (select palette)
products.notes: HARD STOP -- standard dark paint on vinyl causes thermal distortion at ~165 deg F heat deflection (FM-005). IR-reflective pigments allow dark visual colors while reflecting near-infrared radiation. Only 100% acrylic latex binders. Apply thin coats overhead.

material_systems.notes: Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_SFIT_FINISH_SOLAR unchanged. Activated by vinyl substrate + dark color (LRV < 55). When LRV >= 55, standard finish systems are acceptable on vinyl.

SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Acrylic stain-block primer on previously painted wood soffit with localized failures. Spot prime scraped bare areas. Higher coverage than NC bare wood (375 vs 275 SF/gal) because RP substrate is partially sealed by existing paint. Overhead waste factor included.

SS_EXT_PEELING.notes: Acrylic stain-block primer on peeling wood soffit -- full surface prime after heavy scrape. More bare wood exposure = lower coverage than FAILING_PAINT scenario. Overhead waste factor included.

coverage_profiles.overhead_waste_notes: 10% overhead material waste already factored into sf_per_gallon rates above. Do not apply again at runtime.
assumptions: Previously painted substrate -- lower absorption than NC bare wood on intact areas
Spot prime for SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT covers 15-30% of soffit surface (typical localized failure pattern at panel joints and trim junctions)
Full prime for SS_EXT_PEELING covers 100% of surface after heavy scrape
T&G rough-sawn boards: apply surface_texture_modifier 1.15x
Spray application (non-vented only): multiply material quantity by 1.40-1.50x for overhead transfer efficiency loss

coverage_rate.notes: Chalk-binding primer on chalking soffit surface. Full surface application required -- binding must be uniform. Lower coverage (~250 SF/gal) due to thicker-bodied product and aggressive chalk residue absorption. Heavy chalk on south-facing eave edges = low end of range. Overhead waste factor included.

coverage_profiles.overhead_waste_notes: 10% overhead material waste already factored into sf_per_gallon rate above. Do not apply again at runtime.
assumptions: Full surface application mandatory -- chalk binding must be uniform
Low-pressure wash first to remove loose chalk; primer binds remaining residue
Chalk severity drives coverage range: heavy chalk = low end (200 SF/gal), light chalk = high end (300 SF/gal)
Applies to all substrate material types in chalking state
Overhead application of thick-bodied primer increases drip losses

SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare fiber cement soffit areas. Spot prime at failure points. Highly porous bare substrate -- lowest coverage primer in this spec. Overhead waste factor included.

SS_EXT_PEELING.notes: Alkali-resistant primer on extensively exposed bare fiber cement. More bare substrate = greater absorption. Overhead waste factor included.

assumptions: Spot priming exposed bare fiber cement areas only -- not full surface unless extensive failure
Typical bare exposure in RP: 10-30% of soffit surface at panel edge and joint failures
Bare fiber cement is highly porous -- lowest coverage of any primer
Coverage rates match NC COV_SFIT_PRIMER_ALKALI

coverage_rate.notes: PVC bonding primer on exposed bare vinyl soffit areas. Vinyl is non-porous -- consistent higher coverage. Spot prime at failure points. Overhead waste factor included.

assumptions: Spot priming exposed bare vinyl areas only -- not full surface unless extensive failure
Vinyl is non-porous -- coverage is consistent regardless of condition severity
Typical bare exposure in RP: 10-25% of soffit surface
Coverage slightly lower than NC (375 vs 350-400 SF/gal NC) due to overhead waste

SYS_EXT_SFIT_FINISH_STANDARD.notes: Standard acrylic on prepped/primed soffit surface. Primed and prepped RP surface has similar absorption to NC primed surface -- same coverage rate. Overhead waste factor included.

SYS_EXT_SFIT_FINISH_PREMIUM.notes: Premium acrylic has higher solids content -- slightly lower coverage per gallon. Overhead waste factor included.

SYS_EXT_SFIT_FINISH_SOLAR.notes: Solar-reflective formulation with CICP pigments -- reduced coverage vs standard acrylic. Overhead waste factor included.

coverage_profiles.overhead_waste_notes: 10% overhead material waste already factored into sf_per_gallon rates above. Do not apply again at runtime.
assumptions: Coverage is per NET soffit area from PaintScope (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.SOFFIT_FIELD)
Prepped and primed RP surface -- coverage equivalent to NC after prime
Two-coat system at QT3/QT4. QT2 single coat on primed surface.
Spray application (non-vented only): multiply material quantity by 1.40-1.50 for overhead transfer efficiency loss
T&G boards: apply surface_texture_modifier 1.15 for rough-sawn texture. Smooth T&G panels use 1.00.
Reuses NC COV_SFIT_FINISH coverage rates unchanged -- prepped RP surface is equivalent to NC primed surface

consumables.name: RP Assessment Kit (adhesion + chalk + moisture + mildew test)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter, pressure-sensitive tape (ASTM D3359), white cloth for chalk rub test, moisture meter, mildew swab test, biocide assessment supplies
consumables.notes: RP-specific assessment supplies. One kit per project. Includes ASTM D3359 cross-hatch adhesion test, white cloth for chalk rub test, moisture meter for wood panel MC readings at joints and roof penetrations, mildew/algae severity assessment supplies. Shared across exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: Mildewcide / Biocide Solution
consumables.specification: Mildewcide / biocide concentrate (sodium hypochlorite solution or commercial mildew remover), mix per manufacturer directions
consumables.notes: CRITICAL for soffit RP -- mildew is the #1 degradation mechanism for sheltered soffit surfaces. Apply during wash or as separate pre-wash treatment. Kill mildew/algae BEFORE painting -- painting over mildew = guaranteed adhesion failure. Spot treatment for localized mildew; full-surface for widespread mildew. North-facing and shaded soffits require most treatment. Allow 24 hr dry before priming. 1 QT concentrate per ~100 SF of treated surface at typical dilution. Shared across exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Deglosser
consumables.specification: Liquid sander/deglosser, Krud Kutter Gloss-Off or equivalent
consumables.notes: RP-specific: chemical degloss for existing paint on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT soffit. Dulls existing sheen to promote adhesion without full mechanical sanding. Especially useful on overhead surfaces where mechanical sanding is fatiguing. One quart covers ~200 SF of soffit (larger open surface than window profiles). Shared across RP specs.

consumables.name: Carbide Scraper (Exterior Paint Scraping)
consumables.specification: Carbide scraper with replaceable blades, rigid and flexible profiles
consumables.notes: Exterior-specific tool for scraping failing/peeling paint on soffit panels. Carbide blades last longer than steel on exterior paint buildup. Overhead scraping is extremely slow -- gravity works against tool stroke and debris falls on painter. One scraper covers ~500 SF of soffit scraping before blade replacement. Shared across exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: 80-120 Grit Sandpaper for Soffit Prep
consumables.notes: 80-120 grit for feather-edge sanding after scraping on failing/peeling soffit surfaces. Overhead sanding increases consumption -- paper loads faster from gravity-fed dust. Hand blocks for T&G grooves, orbital sander for flat panels. Reused from NC soffit spec.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150 Grit
consumables.notes: General prep sanding on fiber cement soffit and degloss scuffing on sound paint surfaces. Also used for adhesion prep on previously painted surfaces. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 Grit
consumables.notes: Scuff-sand vinyl soffit before bonding primer. Also used for QT4 intercoat sanding between finish coats. Overhead sanding increases consumption. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack Cloth
consumables.notes: Dust removal after sanding before prime or finish coat. Required after all sanding operations. Overhead work causes more dust to fall away from surface -- tack cloth pass ensures clean substrate. Reduced coverage per cloth vs vertical (100 SF overhead vs 150 SF vertical). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Exterior Flexible Paintable Caulk for Soffit Joints
consumables.notes: Polyurethane or siliconized acrylic for soffit panel joints and soffit-to-fascia/frieze junctions. NEVER silicone -- not paintable. In RP, assess caulk condition per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol: intact = paint over, cracked/separated = repair, fully failed = remove and replace. Overhead caulking wastes more per LF due to gravity. Caulk AFTER primer per COMPAT-SFIT-009. Reused from NC soffit spec.

consumables.name: Angled Sash Brush 2.5 inch
consumables.notes: Primary brush for soffit detail -- cut-in at fascia and frieze junctions, T&G groove work, spot priming, edge detail. Overhead brush work demands premium bristle quality. Per convention: 1 brush per material type. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: 9-inch Roller Cover for Overhead Soffit
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 300 SF rolled (primer or finish per coat)
consumables.notes: 3/8-inch nap for smooth soffit panels (plywood, fiber cement, vinyl). 1/2-inch nap for T&G boards. Overhead rolling increases drip losses -- use low-splash covers. Higher consumption rate overhead (300 SF vs 500 SF vertical) due to paint loading and drip losses. Reused from NC soffit spec.

consumables.name: Extension Pole for Overhead Roller Application
consumables.notes: 4-8 ft extension pole attached to roller frame for overhead application from ladder or scaffold. Reduces fatigue and improves coverage consistency. Reusable across projects. Reused from NC soffit spec.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 413 (non-vented soffit only)
consumables.notes: 413-515 tip for soffit spray application on non-vented solid panels ONLY. Spray PROHIBITED on vented soffit (FM-001). Tight to medium fan pattern for controlled overhead application. Overhead spraying increases overspray -- use lower pressure settings. Reused from NC soffit spec.

consumables.name: Painter's Tape (exterior grade UV-resistant 14-day)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum for multi-day exterior projects. Used for fascia edge masking (MANDATORY in RP -- fascia is almost always already finished), frieze masking, light fixture protection, siding edge masking (spray mode), and general edge masking at soffit junctions. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Masking Film/Paper for Adjacent Fascia/Frieze
consumables.notes: Masking film or paper for protecting finished fascia and frieze boards from soffit roller spatter. In RP, adjacent trim is almost always already finished -- protection is MANDATORY (unlike NC where fascia may be unfinished). Tape + 12-inch film along fascia-soffit junction. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Plastic Sheeting for Ground Protection Below Soffit
consumables.notes: 4 mil minimum for landscape and hardscape protection directly below soffit work zone. CRITICAL for overhead RP -- gravity pulls all drips, scraping debris, and wash runoff straight down. Upgraded to full cover for spray mode or when scraping generates debris. Reused from NC soffit spec.

consumables.name: Canvas Drop Cloths
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas drop cloths for hardscape walkway protection below soffit work area. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: 6-Mil Poly Sheeting (RRP Containment)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. 6-mil poly for ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per EPA RRP Rule. WIDER containment than vertical wall work -- overhead scraping debris spreads further. Per-elevation quantity. Shared across all exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: Vent Opening Masking Tape/Foam Plugs
consumables.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: Tape or foam plugs to mask individual soffit vent openings during brush_roll application. Prevents further paint accumulation in vents that may already be partially clogged from prior coats (FM-006). Used on vented soffit RP only. NC vents start clean -- not needed in NC context.

consumables.name: Wire Brush for Vent Cleaning
consumables.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: Wire brush or pick for cleaning paint-clogged vent openings on vented soffit. Used in vent condition assessment and cleaning task. Prior brush_roll coats may have partially clogged perforated vent panels. Restore airflow before re-painting.

ext_landscape_adjacent.description: Landscape area directly below soffit work zone -- drip fallout zone
ext_landscape_adjacent.notes: Ground protection below soffit is MORE critical in RP than NC because scraping generates debris that falls directly down via gravity. Brush/roll GOOD condition: drop cloth at base. Brush/roll FAIR/POOR (scraping): full cover over drip zone. Spray: full tarp coverage. RRP: 6-mil poly per EPA containment rule.

ext_hardscape_walk.description: Adjacent walkways and hardscape directly below soffit work area
ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic on walkways. Plastic sheeting for spray overspray. Overhead drip fallout is heavy -- canvas must be in place before any overhead work begins.

ext_light_fixture.description: Soffit-mounted light fixtures (recessed lights, porch fixtures)
ext_light_fixture.notes: Bag or tape over soffit-mounted fixtures. Remove fixture cover plate if accessible. Same as NC.

ext_fascia_adjacent.description: Fascia board above soffit -- MANDATORY protection in RP (fascia is almost always already finished)
ext_fascia_adjacent.notes: RP upgrade from NC 'when_finished' to 'always' -- in RP context, fascia is almost always already painted. Tape + 12-inch film at fascia-soffit junction prevents roller spatter on finished fascia. No dedicated PaintScope key -- masking quantity derived from soffit perimeter LF.

ext_siding_adjacent.description: Siding field at soffit-to-wall junction (frieze area) -- protect when finished
ext_siding_adjacent.notes: RP upgrade from NC 'when_finished' to 'always' -- in RP context, siding is almost always already painted. Light masking for brush_roll; full masking for spray to prevent overspray on finished siding.

ext_ground_cover.description: General ground protection below soffit work zone for scraping debris
ext_ground_cover.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: Wider coverage than wall-adjacent protection because overhead scraping debris spreads further. Active for SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT and SS_EXT_PEELING conditions where scraping generates debris.

ext_rrp_containment.description: EPA RRP Rule containment for pre-1978 buildings
ext_rrp_containment.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: 6-mil poly extending 10 ft from structure -- WIDER than wall containment for overhead scraping debris spread. Required when pre_1978 + lead. Per-elevation setup/teardown. Shared across all exterior RP specs.

compatibility_rules.description: Sound paint with verified adhesion -- skip prime entirely
compatibility_rules.notes: Existing paint is sound and adhesion verified via ASTM D3359. No primer needed. Degloss/scuff existing surface and proceed to finish coats. Most common soffit RP scenario (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT is the dominant soffit condition due to sheltered location).

compatibility_rules.description: Chalking surface -- chalk-binding primer mandatory (all substrate types)
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY. Topcoat adhesion failure guaranteed without chalk-binding step. Full surface application required regardless of substrate material type. Applies after low-pressure wash and 24-48 hour dry time. Less common on soffit than siding/trim (sheltered from UV) but occurs on south-facing exposed eave-edge soffits.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing/peeling paint on wood -- acrylic stain-block RP primer on exposed areas
compatibility_rules.notes: Acrylic stain-block primer on bare wood areas. Spot prime localized failures; full prime when SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread bare exposure. Seal all exposed wood grain.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing/peeling paint on fiber cement -- alkali-resistant primer on exposed areas
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY on exposed bare fiber cement (pH 13.0). Prevents saponification. Spot prime exposed areas. Also requires general RP primer (acrylic stain-block or chalk-binding) on painted areas if those areas also need prime.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing/peeling paint on vinyl -- PVC bonding primer on exposed areas
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY on exposed bare vinyl. Standard primers will NOT bond to vinyl -- peeling within 6-12 months. Clean and scuff-sand vinyl before application. Recoat within 1 week. Spot prime exposed areas.

compatibility_rules.description: Mildew present -- biocide treatment mandatory before any coating

then.sequence: biocide treatment -> 24 hr dry -> low-pressure wash -> 24-48 hr dry -> prime/paint

compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY. Mildew is the #1 degradation concern for soffit surfaces. Painting over mildew causes guaranteed adhesion failure. Kill mildew with biocide BEFORE painting. Soffit is especially prone due to sheltered, shaded, damp conditions.

compatibility_rules.description: Spray application PROHIBITED on vented soffit
compatibility_rules.notes: HARD RULE unchanged from NC. Spray on vented soffit drives atomized paint into attic through vent perforations. Contaminates insulation, clogs vent screens, reduces ventilation capacity. Brush/roll only on vented soffits. FM-001.

compatibility_rules.description: Vinyl soffit with dark color (LRV < 55) -- VinylSafe IR-reflective finish required

then.notes: HARD STOP -- standard dark paint on vinyl causes thermal distortion. Solar-reflective IR coating is NON-NEGOTIABLE.

compatibility_rules.description: Only 100% acrylic latex binders on vinyl soffit
compatibility_rules.notes: Transfers unchanged from NC. Alkyd/oil binders become brittle on vinyl substrate. COMPAT-SFIT-007.

compatibility_rules.description: Flat and satin sheen only for soffit
compatibility_rules.notes: Transfers unchanged from NC. Overhead surfaces show imperfections at higher sheen. COMPAT-SFIT-008.

compatibility_rules.description: No power washing on soffit -- low-pressure wash only
compatibility_rules.notes: Transfers from NC. High-pressure power washing PROHIBITED on soffit. Damages thin panel edges, forces water into attic through vent openings, strips paint film. Low-pressure wash only (500-800 PSI max, fan tip, mildew detergent). COMPAT-SFIT-010.

compatibility_rules.description: Caulk AFTER primer coat -- never before
compatibility_rules.notes: Transfers from NC. Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces. COMPAT-SFIT-009.

compatibility_rules.description: Vented soffit RP -- mask vent openings during brush_roll application

then.notes: Mask individual vent openings to prevent further paint accumulation in vents

compatibility_rules.notes: RP-SPECIFIC. Prior brush_roll coats may have partially clogged vent perforations. Masking during RP prevents additional paint buildup. Not needed in NC (vents start clean).

risk_notes.topic: Mildew adhesion failure from painting over untreated mildew
risk_notes.risk: Mildew is the #1 degradation mechanism for soffit. Painting over untreated mildew causes complete adhesion failure within 6-12 months -- new paint film peels in sheets. Soffit is highest-risk exterior surface for mildew due to sheltered, shaded, damp conditions.
risk_notes.mitigation: MANDATORY biocide treatment before painting. Kill mildew, wash residue, allow 24 hr dry. Use mildew-resistant paint formulation. Verify mildew is dead (no dark spots under wash).

risk_notes.topic: Attic vent contamination from spray on vented soffit
risk_notes.risk: Spray application on vented soffit drives atomized paint into attic through perforated panels or vent openings. Contaminates insulation, clogs vent screens, reduces ventilation capacity.
risk_notes.mitigation: HARD RULE: Brush/roll only on vented soffits. Spray only on non-vented solid panel soffits. FM-001.

risk_notes.topic: Thermal distortion on vinyl soffit from dark paint
risk_notes.risk: Standard dark paint (LRV < 55) on vinyl soffit absorbs excessive heat, causing PVC panels to warp, buckle, or permanently deform at ~165 deg F.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use solar-reflective (VinylSafe) coating on ALL vinyl soffit with color LRV < 55. HARD STOP. FM-005.

risk_notes.topic: Lead dust exposure from overhead scraping on pre-1978 soffit
risk_notes.risk: Overhead scraping on pre-1978 soffit sends lead paint chips and dust directly downward via gravity onto crew and ground. MORE hazardous than vertical scraping because debris falls onto the painter.
risk_notes.mitigation: RRP containment (6-mil poly 10 ft from structure). Wet scraping methods. HEPA vacuum for sanding. Full PPE. Wider containment zone than vertical wall work.

risk_notes.topic: Chalking adhesion failure from skipping chalk-binding primer
risk_notes.risk: Topcoating directly over chalking soffit surface without chalk-binding primer causes complete adhesion failure. New paint peels in sheets when chalk layer separates from substrate.
risk_notes.mitigation: MANDATORY chalk-binding primer on SS_EXT_CHALKING. Full surface application. No exceptions.

risk_notes.topic: Overhead paint drip and sag on soffit
risk_notes.risk: Overhead application makes paint drips and sags highly visible and difficult to control. Excess material runs to fascia junction or drips onto surfaces and crew below.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply thin coats overhead. Back-brush immediately after rolling. Use extension pole for consistent pressure. Protect all surfaces below before beginning overhead work.

risk_notes.topic: Bonding primer over-exposure on vinyl soffit
risk_notes.risk: Bonding primer left exposed beyond 1 week dries brittle -- loses flexibility needed for topcoat adhesion bond on vinyl.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply topcoat within 1 week of bonding primer application. If exceeded, scuff-sand before topcoat. RISK-SFIT-008.

risk_notes.topic: Vent clogging from repeated paint application
risk_notes.risk: Repeated brush_roll applications on vented soffit progressively clog vent perforations with paint, reducing attic ventilation capacity.
risk_notes.mitigation: Mask vent openings during application (CON_SFRP_VENT_MASK_TAPE). Clean paint-clogged vents with wire brush during assessment. Note heavily clogged vents for homeowner -- recommend replacement.

material_quantity_notes.overhead_waste_factor: All soffit coverage rates already include ~10% overhead waste factor (gravity-fed dripping, application angle inefficiency). Do NOT apply additional overhead waste at runtime.
material_quantity_notes.surface_texture_factor: T&G rough-sawn boards: multiply material quantity by 1.15x for texture absorption. Smooth panels (plywood, FC, vinyl): 1.00x.
material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on non-vented soffit: 50-60% transfer efficiency overhead (worse than vertical 65-75%). Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.40-1.50. Overhead spraying has worse transfer efficiency than vertical -- lean toward 1.50.
material_quantity_notes.coat_system_rp: RP coat system varies by condition: GOOD = 2 finish only (QT3/QT4) or 1 finish (QT2). FAIR/POOR = state-driven prime + finish coats. QT2 FAIR/POOR = prime + 1 finish. QT3/QT4 FAIR/POOR = prime + 2 finish.
material_quantity_notes.spot_prime_coverage: Spot prime area estimate: SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT = 15-30% of soffit surface (localized at panel joints and trim junctions). SS_EXT_PEELING = 40-60%+ (often moisture-driven from above). Calculate material from spot area, not total soffit SF.

assumptions.value: 325-375 SF/gal for acrylic RP primer on previously painted soffit
assumptions.source: NC COV_SFIT_PRIMER adjusted: previously painted substrate absorbs less, but overhead waste increases consumption
assumptions.note: Previously painted substrate (intact areas) absorbs less primer than bare wood. Net effect: higher SF/gal than NC bare wood (275 SF/gal) but with overhead waste included.

assumptions.value: 200-300 SF/gal for chalk-binding primer on chalking soffit
assumptions.source: SF_WINDOW_EXT_RP_v1 COV_XWRP_PRIMER_CHALK_BIND (275 SF/gal) adjusted for overhead waste and soffit-specific chalk patterns
assumptions.note: Chalk-binding primer is thicker-bodied with lower coverage. Overhead application increases drip losses for thick product.

assumptions.value: 250-350 SF/gal for finish coat on prepped/primed soffit
assumptions.source: NC COV_SFIT_FINISH (300 SF/gal standard, 275 SF/gal premium) -- same rates apply because prepped RP surface is equivalent to NC primed surface
assumptions.note: Finish coat coverage on prepped/primed RP surface matches NC primed surface. Overhead waste factor already included in NC rates.

assumptions.value: Biocide treatment expected on majority of soffit RP projects
assumptions.source: Research RF-005: mildew is the PRIMARY degradation mechanism for sheltered soffit
assumptions.note: No doctrine specifies mildew treatment frequency for soffit RP. Field experience indicates >60% of soffit RP projects require at least spot mildew treatment. Material estimate should include biocide as standard consumable, not conditional.

uncertainty_flags.description: The 15-30% spot prime area estimate for SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT is based on typical soffit failure patterns (panel joints, trim junctions). Actual area varies significantly by project. POOR condition projects may have 40-60%+ bare exposure.
uncertainty_flags.action: Flag for field calibration. Track actual scraped/exposed area as percentage of total soffit SF on RP projects.

uncertainty_flags.description: Overhead spray transfer efficiency (50-60%) is estimated -- worse than vertical (65-75%). Limited data for overhead spray on soffit specifically.
uncertainty_flags.action: Flag for field calibration when spray on non-vented soffit is actually performed. Limited data -- uncommon scenario.

uncertainty_flags.description: Biocide solution coverage rate (1 QT per 100 SF) varies by dilution ratio and mildew severity. Heavy mildew may require double application.
uncertainty_flags.action: Track actual biocide consumption per project. Standardize dilution ratio in SOP.

uncertainty_flags.description: Chalk-binding primer coverage on overhead soffit is estimated at 250 SF/gal (range 200-300). Thick-bodied product drips more overhead. Limited field data for chalk-binding primer specifically on soffit.
uncertainty_flags.action: Track actual material consumption on chalking soffit RP projects.
